title: Why Cash Sitting Still Is Quietly Losing Value
description:
$10,000 in a drawer for 20 years - the number never changes, but what it can buy does. We show how average inflation erodes the real value of cash left idle, and compare it against a basic savings account and long-term investing.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#inflation #purchasingpower #personalfinance

segments.text: Ten thousand dollars sitting in a drawer for twenty years. The number on it never changes. What it can buy does.
Inflation doesn't take money out of your account. It just makes every dollar in it worth a little less, every single year.
At an average of three and a half percent inflation, prices roughly double every twenty years.
So that same ten thousand dollars, left untouched, loses roughly half its real buying power in two decades.
Move that same money into a basic savings account paying one percent, and it barely helps. You're still losing ground to inflation every year.
Only real growth, above the inflation rate, actually protects what your money can buy.

slide.headline: Real purchasing power of $10,000 after 20 years

segments.text: Sitting still doesn't feel risky. But against inflation, doing nothing is still a choice, and it's usually the expensive one.
Cash feels safe. It just isn't neutral.
